title: Mozilla, Google, Apple block compromised eMudhra CA certificates
description: The certificate authority eMudhra revoked eight compromised intermediate certificates after researchers discovered their private keys were extremely weak, allowing near-instant recovery and potential forgery of trusted certificates. Major browsers including Mozilla, Google, and Apple have blocked these compromised certificates to prevent misuse.
aiSummary: Researchers identified that eight intermediate certificates issued by the certificate authority eMudhra had private keys so weak that attackers could recover them almost instantly. This weakness enables attackers to forge trusted certificates for legitimate websites, undermining the trust model of TLS/SSL. In response, eMudhra revoked the affected intermediate certificates, and major browser vendors such as Mozilla, Google, and Apple have blocked these certificates to protect users from potential man-in-the-middle attacks or impersonation.
aiImpact: The compromised intermediate certificates could allow attackers to issue fraudulent certificates trusted by browsers, potentially enabling man-in-the-middle attacks or impersonation of legitimate websites. This undermines the security of TLS connections relying on these certificates. However, the revocation and blocking by major browsers mitigate the risk of exploitation.
